Leftover 5-12k peaks now +0.4 to +0.7 dB; the 15.8k peak fully served (worst 14-17k residual now -1.8 dip-side).

turns.complaint: You're the new EQ Assistant working on the ZMF Ori 3.0! Here's my complaint: the treble is *improved*, but it's not *corrected*. I think we're over-fitting/shaping in the treble and it's causing phase issues among other problems. Take a look at the Auteur Classics tuning and the ZMF Blackwood's current treble tunings: they're tracing the general shape of the raw measurements, but they're not fitting every sub-db peak either. What do you propose we do about that to get the treble from "improved" to "corrected" so I can get the air/space/depth I'm craving?
turns.clarify: Phase half of the complaint adjudicated against the corpus before proposing: minimum-phase EQ is the minimum-dispersion realisation of its magnitude (PHASE.md), and the v5 chain's worst bands compute to ~0.19-0.23 ms peak group delay (tau ~ 0.225*Q/f0), under every published audibility threshold, with narrow-band delay the least audible kind. Phase declined as mechanism; magnitude misalignment and overdrive accepted instead. User approved the plan: broad-Q refit at 1/6 oct, sub-1 dB features dropped, no-overshoot guards, 15.5k depth capped, magnitude ladder for by-ear scaling.

diagnosis.method: search+refine over the five v5 treble bands (replace, f fixed at measured centres, Q boxed <=4 below 10k / <=3.5 above, 15.5k gain capped -6) against the same 1/6-oct tilted-DF difference target; guards: canyon dev >= -8.5, |mean 2700-5200| <= 0.75, per-region maxdev floors -1.75. Constraint design iterated: absolute floors first (infeasible - canyon skirt in the 9-12k window), then mean floors (binding on the very peaks being cut), settled on maxdev backstops with the ERB-weighted rmse objective as the balance judge. Jobs sessions/ori/ori3-treble-discipline.json; final chain verified by evaluate against the literal v5 tail.
diagnosis.finding: Three real defects in v5: (1) overshoot past target - 9-12k dev +2.9 -> -2.27 and 14-17k +4.6 -> -1.83, both regions driven below target, on top of the untouched 12-14k canyon: the 9-17k band (air) was net depressed; (2) Q 8.4 / 9.8 cuts with ~1 kHz half-gain bandwidths placed against a factory 5128 coupler curve above the reliability ceiling - centres indicative only, so in-ear the cuts part-miss their peaks and dig fresh dips; (3) -10.2 dB at 15.5k sized from unsmoothed height of a top-octave coupler feature. Physics found by the search: the Ori treble is tall peaks over valleys already at target, so any broad cut deep enough to null a peak tip drags a valley 2-3 dB under - v5's high-Q surgery was the solver's escape from that tension, and the broad refit instead leaves peak tips +1 to +4 unserved as the price of broadness. Refit result: four cuts Q 2.6-4.0, rmse_erb 5-12k 1.05 vs v5's 1.18 - broad beats surgical even on paper. The 11.6k band refined to -0.5 dB (below the 1 dB feature floor) and was dropped.
diagnosis.explains_symptom: "improved but not corrected" = high-Q cuts part-missing in-ear resonances while their misses read as new colouration; missing "air/space/depth" = the 9-17k net depression from overshoot plus the canyon. Not phase: computed group delay sits well under every published threshold.
